_comment: An order squares a block whose ranks stand near a quarter-turn off its heading by dealing the ranks again at the quarter, then turning out only the few degrees left (#1865). A 60-man Infantry block (10 files by 6 ranks) stands on Hold facing north at (620, 540). A brittle 20-man Infantry block (morale 1, all_teams_control, ordered at tick 14) attacks it from the east. On contact (about tick 340) the block turns in place to face its attacker, and the turn settles into the fold, so its ranks stand 85.0 degrees off its heading. The attacker routs at about tick 528 and the block is out of contact and idle by tick 638, its heading at 20.4 degrees. At tick 724 the player orders it 300 wu along that heading. Measured on Windows against main 47a316a0 with FULL dumps every 2 ticks from 700 to 1000. On main the order turned the whole 85-degree fold out after the heading at the bounded rate: the ranks still stood 84.9 degrees off at tick 730 and 69.9 at tick 800, and came square only at about tick 980, so the block set off crabwise; between ticks 722 and 1000 each man walked 91.9 wu on average about the block's anchor and 16 of the 60 ended across the centreline from where they began. Here the order deals the ranks again at the quarter from where the men stand, so the ranks stand 5.0 degrees off at tick 724, 4.9 at 730 and 0.2 at 800; each man walks 41.2 wu on average and none crosses the centreline. A fold 5 degrees past the quarter is dealt again at the same quarter and turns out 5 degrees the other way, where main reflected the block by a half-turn and wheeled it nearly a quarter-turn back. The tick-730 and tick-800 grid_off_heading expects fail on main.
